The Makurdi Processing Plant is the cooperative's primary cassava processing facility. The plant was acquired as a complete line from a defunct agro-processing firm in Otukpo, with the equipment reconditioned and reinstalled at the current site. This record consolidates the original acquisition specifications with the verified 2025 operating parameters. The plant has operated continuously since commissioning, with the exception of scheduled shutdowns and one extended closure from 10-07-2023 to 05-08-2023 following the flood damage to the access road and the electrical substation.

1. PLANT CAPACITY (VERIFIED 2025)

This is the design capacity of the peeling, washing, chipping, and drying line, and it remains the figure used for all production planning, raw material procurement, and sales forecasting. No capacity upgrade or debottlenecking has been undertaken since commissioning; the 20 MT/day figure is unchanged from the original manufacturer's specification sheet (see Section 2 below).

During the 2024 harvest season, the plant operated at an average of 17.5 MT/day due to staffing constraints, but this was an operational issue, not a change in plant capacity.

The plant processes fresh cassava roots into high-quality cassava flour (HQCF) and, on a campaign basis, gari. The following are the average yields recorded during the 2024 operating year (January–December 2024). These are actual recorded yields, not design values.

- Down time (scheduled maintenance and cleaning): 34 days
- Unscheduled down time (breakdowns, power failures): 12 days

DETAILED REPORT FOR 28-01-2025 SCHEDULED MAINTENANCE (MKT-PLT-GEN)

The scheduled maintenance on 28-01-2025 was the first full-plant shutdown of the year. The shutdown began at 08:00 and the plant was handed back to the Production Manager at 17:30. The following tasks were completed during this shutdown:

1. Full lubrication of all drive chains and bearings on the peeling line, chipping machine, and press.
2. Inspection and retensioning of all conveyor belts.
3. Replacement of the worn discharge hose on the hammer mill (MKT-MIL-01).
4. Calibration of the moisture meter used for HQCF quality checks.
5. Deep cleaning of the flash dryer ducting.
6. Electrical inspection of all control panels and safety cut-outs.

No major faults were found. The maintenance crew noted that the bearing on the feed auger (MKT-AUG-01) is beginning to show signs of wear and has been scheduled for replacement during the next planned shutdown. This is a routine observation, not an emergency.

SECTION 10: PLANT ASSET RECORD — MAKURDI PROCESSING PLANT (ACQUISITION AND CURRENT SPECIFICATION)

The Makurdi Processing Plant is the cooperative's primary cassava processing facility. The plant was acquired as a complete line from a defunct agro-processing firm in Otukpo, with the equipment reconditioned and reinstalled at the current site. This record consolidates the original acquisition specifications with the verified 2025 operating parameters. The plant has operated continuously since commissioning, with the exception of scheduled shutdowns and one extended closure from 10-07-2023 to 05-08-2023 following the flood damage to the access road and the electrical substation.

1. PLANT CAPACITY (VERIFIED 2025)

Makurdi Processing Plant processing_capacity is 20 metric tons per day. Record status: current. Record status: current — verified during the 2025 annual asset audit (conducted 10-02-2025 to 14-02-2025). This is the design capacity of the peeling, washing, chipping, and drying line, and it remains the figure used for all production planning, raw material procurement, and sales forecasting. No capacity upgrade or debottlenecking has been undertaken since commissioning; the 20 MT/day figure is unchanged from the original manufacturer's specification sheet (see Section 2 below).

2. ORIGINAL ACQUISITION SPECIFICATIONS (AS INSTALLED, 2019)

The following specifications were recorded at installation and are retained for reference. They are the original values, not current operating parameters. Where a parameter has been verified as unchanged, the verification date is noted.

Note: The peeling station is manual and is the current bottleneck in practice. The rated capacity of 20 MT/day is achievable with the full 12-station staff complement. During the 2024 harvest season, the plant operated at an average of 17.5 MT/day due to staffing constraints, but this was an operational issue, not a change in plant capacity.

3. PROCESS FLOW AND YIELD DATA (2024 OPERATING YEAR)

The plant processes fresh cassava roots into high-quality cassava flour (HQCF) and, on a campaign basis, gari. The following are the average yields recorded during the 2024 operating year (January–December 2024). These are actual recorded yields, not design values.

- Fresh roots received: 4,850 MT

Yield data is recorded on a daily basis in the Plant Production Log (Form BVC-PRD-04). The 2024 figures above are the aggregate of the daily logs and have been reconciled with the sales records by the internal audit unit.

The machine was delivered to the cooperative yard on 12-04-2024 and offloaded the same day. Installation was done by the supplier's technical team over 14-16 April 2024. The mill was bolted to a reinforced concrete plinth (1.2 m high) to keep the feed hopper at a comfortable working height for the operators. A dedicated 100 kVA transformer was installed the previous month to handle the motor's starting current. The machine was test-run on 17-04-2024 with dry cassava chips and then with wet roots; both runs were satisfactory. The cooperatives safety officer inspected the guards and emergency stop buttons before the mill was released for production on 18-04-2024.

**SPECIFICATIONS AND OPERATING PARAMETERS**

The CM-5000 is a hammer-type mill with a stainless steel grinding chamber. It is fitted with a 3 mm screen for HQCF production and a 5 mm screen for gari flour. The feed auger (MKT-AUG-01) is driven off the main motor via a reduction gearbox. The mill's rated throughput is 5,000 kg/hr, but the Production Manager has noted that actual throughput during the 2024 season averaged 4,200-4,600 kg/hr depending on the moisture content of the roots. The machine has a manual reversing switch for clearing blockages in the grinding chamber. Operators have been trained on the correct start-up sequence: check oil level in gearbox, turn on dust extraction, start the auger, then start the main motor.
